semantic_adjudication.reason: The predicate S3 (trigger_set_equals) completed with verdict=false, producing a counterexample: expected={frontend collision detected, rear-end collision detected, collision with pedestrian detected} vs. observed={Possible_collision_detected}. The exact model facts confirm that transition:line:32 is the sole entry edge to CA and carries only the event Possible_collision_detected. The three specific events (Frontend_collision_detected, Rear_end_collision_detected, Pedestrian_collision_detected) are declared in the model but appear only on internal transitions within CA's sub-states, not on the entry edge. This establishes a first reading in which the entry trigger set does not match the NL2-required set. However, a competing semantic reading remains compatible with the same facts: the NL2 clause uses 'possible' as a collective modifier before enumerating three collision types, and the model's single entry event 'Possible_collision_detected' can be read as the author's intentional abstraction of that collective condition, with the specific events handling internal dispatch. No supplied fact explicitly excludes this abstraction reading (there is no NL clause requiring the entry edge to carry exactly the three specific event names, and no formal mapping ties Possible_collision_detected to a disjunction of the three). Therefore the undercutting defeater survives: two competent trigger-set readings remain compatible with the same exact facts.

The NL1 text uses 'region' without the UML-specific qualifier 'orthogonal' that would unambiguously select the concurrent-region reading, leaving the child-state reading as a semantically viable alternative for the same sentence.

issues.reason: The contract's binding hints explicitly list three triggers (frontend collision detected, rear-end collision detected, collision with pedestrian detected) for the CA entry. The complete closed transition inventory shows only one entry edge to CA (transition:line:32) with a different single trigger. issues.expected: CA should contain orthogonal regions (UML --- separators) partitioning the three collision avoidance controls (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) into concurrently active regions, enabling simultaneous activation of different controls.

The canonical_source_ir confirms concurrent_regions count=0. The FCSTM text shows all three sub-composites in one sequential block within CA. issues.reason: NL3 explicitly requires 'orthogonal regions' for 'concurrent activation' of the three collision avoidance controls. The complete source and model inventories show no region separators (---) within CA; all three sub-composites are in a single implicit region. The canonical IR independently confirms concurrent_regions=0. This is a precise structural absence with exact owner and member identities.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The author may have intended the three sub-states to operate concurrently by convention or external orchestration, relying on the NL description rather than explicit UML region syntax. The PlantUML nesting without separators could be a notational omission rather than a semantic choice.

issues.basis: NL2 activation obligation; FCSTM line:30 [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial (scope=CA); working_contract identifying compiler:state:llms_emp_feedback_final_0057.CA.UnspecifiedInitial as synthetic_state; verify_facts non_proved entries refuting reachability of state:Frontend:line:8, state:RearEnd:line:15, state:Pedestrian:line:22 and all their children; inspection_equivalent_facts LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic on UnspecifiedInitial; PlantUML source showing no [*] arrow at CA level.
issues.expected: CA's internal default entry should route to its operational sub-states (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) or properly initialize concurrent regions, enabling the sub-machine to become active and execute collision avoidance behavior upon entry.
issues.observed: CA's only internal initial edge (transition:line:30, [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial) targets a compiler-synthetic placeholder state with zero outgoing transitions. The author specified no CA-level default entry in the PlantUML source. All three functional sub-composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) and their children are unreachable from any initial entry, confirmed by verify_facts refuting reachability for all nine operational states. The system enters CA via the root-level conditional edge but immediately lands in the dead-end UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.reason: NL2 requires the sub-machine to 'become active,' which is impossible when its internal default entry targets a synthetic dead-end. The author did not specify any CA-level default entry in the PlantUML source; the compiler generated [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial as a fallback. The deterministic reachability facts confirm that no operational state within CA is reachable. This is a distinct initial_entry violation from the region_structure and trigger_set issues: even if the trigger and region structure were corrected, the internal initialization would still fail to route to functional behavior.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: If CA were structured with proper orthogonal regions (as NL3 requires), each region would have its own independent initial pseudostate, and CA would not need a single top-level default entry. The absence of a CA-level functional default entry could be a consequence of the missing region structure rather than an independent defect. However, even under the current single-region interpretation, the default entry must reach a functional child for the sub-machine to be operable.
issues.title: CA internal default entry targets synthetic dead-end UnspecifiedInitial; all operational sub-states unreachable

issues.basis: verify_facts: reachability refuted for state:Frontend:line:8, state:RearEnd:line:15, state:Pedestrian:line:22 and all children; inspection reachable_state_refs=[root, CA, UnspecifiedInitial] only; CA initial entry transition:line:30 (source=[*], target=UnspecifiedInitial, triggers=[], scope=CA); UnspecifiedInitial has outgoing_transition_refs=[] (dead leaf); source tr_0001/tr_0004/tr_0007 confirm valid internal initial edges exist in each sub-composite
issues.expected: CA's operational sub-composites (Frontend, RearEnd, Pedestrian) must be reachable from the root initial entry so the collision avoidance sub-machine can be behaviorally active
issues.observed: All three sub-composites and their six child states are unreachable from the top-level initial entry; CA's only initial edge (transition:line:30) targets the compiler-synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state which has zero outgoing transitions, creating a dead end that prevents entry to any operational sub-composite
issues.reason: The verify facts refute reachability for all nine operational states. The root cause is CA's initial entry (transition:line:30) targeting the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial dead state. The behavior_consequence lens derives this because NL2's requirement for an active sub-machine is behaviorally void if its operational states cannot be reached from root. G1 checks path existence from root to Frontend (representative); the same refutation applies to RearEnd and Pedestrian.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Each sub-composite has a valid internal initial edge to its Idle state (tr_0001: [*]->FCIdle, tr_0004: [*]->RCIdle, tr_0007: [*]->PCIdle); if CA's initial entry were corrected to target any operational sub-composite, all internal states would become reachable. The unreachability is solely due to CA's missing valid initial entry, not a structural deficiency in the sub-composites themselves.
issues.title: All three CA operational sub-composites unreachable from root initial entry

issues.basis: verify_facts: event-consumer refuted for Frontend_collision_detected (consumer transition:line:12, reachable=[]), Rear_end_collision_detected (consumer transition:line:19, reachable=[]), Pedestrian_collision_detected (consumer transition:line:26, reachable=[]); inspection event_consumers confirm declared consumers with empty reachable sets; source tr_0002 (FCIdle->FCActive on Frontend collision detected), tr_0005 (RCIdle->RCActive on Rear-end collision detected), tr_0008 (PCIdle->PCActive on Pedestrian collision detected)
issues.expected: Each of the three collision detection events must have at least one reachable consumer transition within CA's operating scope for the sub-machine to respond to collisions
issues.observed: All three events have exactly one declared consumer each (transition:line:12 for Frontend, transition:line:19 for Rear-end, transition:line:26 for Pedestrian) but zero reachable consumers from the top-level initial entry; all consumer states (FCIdle, RCIdle, PCIdle) are unreachable
issues.reason: The verify facts independently refute event-consumer reachability for all three collision events. The inspection facts confirm each event has declared consumers with empty reachable_consumer_transition_refs. This is a distinct behavioral property from root reachability: it specifically verifies that the event-to-consumer operational linkage is available, not merely that states exist in the model. The frozen predicate registry has no dedicated event-consumer-coverage predicate, so this remains predicate-null W1.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The consumer transitions exist and are correctly structured (Idle->Active on collision event); if the upstream reachability defect (CA initial entry to dead synthetic state) were repaired, all consumers would become reachable. The event-consumer coverage failure is a direct consequence of the initial-entry defect rather than an independent missing consumer linkage.
